scenarios.given: each selected language on a supported platform with a declared project fixture
scenarios.then: status identifies exact versions and prerequisites; core symbol/definition/reference/hover/diagnostic/rename fixtures pass and a representative edit-based action is qualified.

scenarios.given: a missing, incompatible or unlicensed provider
scenarios.when: semantic setup or a query is requested
scenarios.then: the cause and actionable setup path appear; no unsupported feature is advertised and structural graph/memory remain usable.

scenarios.given: an installed provider and an interrupted upgrade
scenarios.then: the exact configured version is usable or a recoverable failure is shown; no surprise download, shell hook or duplicate installation occurs.

scenarios.given: two classes expose the same method name, with aliases and typed call sites
scenarios.when: definition and references are requested for one occurrence
scenarios.then: the qualified provider resolves the correct declaration and references without including the unrelated method merely by name.

scenarios.given: an ambiguous locator or a stale graph handle
scenarios.then: candidates or a stale/unresolved result are returned; no arbitrary symbol is presented as exact.

scenarios.given: a provider supports completion and hierarchy but lacks one requested feature
scenarios.then: supported results retain their observation identity; the unsupported operation is explicit rather than an empty successful result.

scenarios.given: existing diagnostics and a new edit
scenarios.then: new/resolved/remaining items refer to the requested view and version; delayed older diagnostics cannot replace them.

scenarios.given: a task targets a symbol with one current constraint, one stale decision and unrelated memory
scenarios.when: context is requested within a budget
scenarios.then: current relevant evidence and its applicable constraint are included; stale evidence is labeled, unrelated material omitted, and omissions are visible.

scenarios.given: no applicable memory or an unreviewed proposal is linked to a symbol
scenarios.then: code evidence remains useful; no fabricated constraint appears and proposals retain their unapproved status.

scenarios.given: two worktrees have the same paths and different code
scenarios.then: each receives evidence from its own worktree/configuration without buffer, cache or memory-scope contamination.

scenarios.given: two clients hold different unsaved text for the same file
scenarios.when: they query or propose an edit
scenarios.then: their explicit views stay distinct; conflicting edit ownership is rejected without choosing the last writer silently.

scenarios.given: a document changes after a request starts
scenarios.then: it cannot be labeled current for the new version; the response exposes stale/conflict status or a bounded retry.

scenarios.given: project configuration, dependency version or branch changes
scenarios.then: the obsolete analysis basis is invalidated; current project identity is used or readiness is reported explicitly.

scenarios.given: a cold provider, a hung request and another healthy workspace
scenarios.then: the request finishes within the exposed budget semantics, resources are released, and the healthy workspace continues without unlimited retry or spawning.

scenarios.given: a provider crashes repeatedly or fails graceful shutdown
scenarios.then: bounded restart/escalation, cause and next action are visible; abandoned processes do not remain as unbounded resource leaks.

scenarios.given: separate cases of zero references, incomplete project load, unsupported feature and timeout
scenarios.then: the four outcomes are distinguishable in machine-readable and compact forms; none falsely proves repository-wide absence.

scenarios.given: a large reference set with a fixed observation
scenarios.when: bounded pages or compact output are requested
scenarios.then: each page obeys its limits and retains source/coverage metadata; continuation retrieves the same set without duplicates or unexplained loss.

scenarios.given: a continuation cursor refers to an earlier observation
scenarios.when: source or scope changes before the next page
scenarios.then: the cursor is rejected or explicitly rebound by a new query, never used to mix snapshots.

scenarios.given: a repository requests build import, macro execution or dependency download outside the granted policy
scenarios.then: the operation is blocked or routed through existing authorization; limited analysis is labeled and no repository text grants itself permission.

scenarios.given: a selected symbol has references across several files
scenarios.then: the proposal identifies every provider-returned change and precondition with a full retrievable diff; all source bytes remain unchanged.

scenarios.given: a code action changes text and renames or deletes a resource
scenarios.then: the complete ordered operation set and effects are visible; unsupported resource operations are rejected before application.

scenarios.given: a complete proposal covered by the task authorization and matching current preconditions
scenarios.then: only the specified targets change and a result receipt identifies the proposal and resulting observations; no redundant permission request is required.

scenarios.given: one target changes, becomes read-only, escapes the authorized root through a symlink, or loses authorization before apply
scenarios.then: the whole preflight is rejected with a concrete conflict and no target is changed.

scenarios.given: an edit targets an unsaved editor-owned buffer
scenarios.then: the owner acknowledges the versioned edit or rejects it; Threadnote never bypasses the buffer by blindly rewriting disk.

scenarios.given: an application acknowledgement is lost after some or all writes
scenarios.when: the caller retries the same operation
scenarios.then: the operation is reconciled against recorded intent and actual versions; it is not applied twice and an unknown outcome is not labeled success.

scenarios.given: a process interruption or disk failure occurs mid-application and the user later edits one target
scenarios.then: changed and unchanged targets are reported, recovery is reviewable, and later edits are preserved; partial/indeterminate status persists until reconciled.

scenarios.given: a provider returns an opaque shell command or unqualified command identifier
scenarios.when: the caller asks for that code action
scenarios.then: the command is rejected with supported alternatives; no arbitrary process execution occurs.

scenarios.given: a successful rename moves a previously cited symbol
scenarios.when: context and diagnostics are requested again
scenarios.then: old results are invalidated; verified relocation or explicit unresolved status is shown and durable memory is not silently rewritten.

scenarios.given: a standard client negotiates UTF-8 or UTF-16 and opens Unicode/CRLF documents
scenarios.when: sync, navigation and cancellation are exercised
scenarios.then: ranges round-trip correctly, synchronization is ordered, unsupported capabilities are not advertised and stdout remains valid LSP framing.

scenarios.given: VS Code or Cursor already has a native language extension
scenarios.when: Threadnote is installed in default coexistence mode
scenarios.then: Threadnote knowledge is available without duplicate completion/diagnostic/refactoring providers; semantic ownership changes only through explicit setup.

scenarios.given: a generic LSP client with no Threadnote-specific UI extension
scenarios.when: the documented stdio configuration is used
scenarios.then: standard advertised navigation/hover features work; custom knowledge affordances are clearly optional and unsupported methods fail coherently.

scenarios.given: a symbol has private, shared and out-of-scope memories
scenarios.when: an editor renders knowledge hover or CodeLens
scenarios.then: only authorized relevant records appear with freshness and navigable links; rendering does not publish them or expose unrelated private data.

scenarios.given: the same project/view/request is submitted through CLI JSON and MCP without an editor
scenarios.when: results or an edit proposal are retrieved
scenarios.then: evidence, capability/error meaning and guarded-edit preconditions agree; transport presentation may differ without semantic loss.

scenarios.given: a monorepo has multiple roots and two versions of a dependency
scenarios.then: the correct project/version is identified; references and graph impact expose their respective scope and do not claim exhaustive cross-repository runtime impact.

scenarios.given: source or provider diagnostics contain credentials or private text
scenarios.when: status, logs or telemetry are exported by default
scenarios.then: content and secrets are omitted/redacted; intended source-bearing responses remain confined to the authorized caller.

scenarios.given: an existing Threadnote 5 workspace with memories, citations and offline graph use
scenarios.when: 6.0 is installed and semantic analysis stays disabled or is later disabled
scenarios.then: existing context remains accessible; no semantic runtime or permanent daemon is required and configuration removal does not delete user content.

scenarios.given: a previous client or incompatible cache/version accesses the upgraded service
scenarios.when: a request or rollback is attempted
scenarios.then: supported contracts remain available or a precise incompatibility/recovery path is returned; no memory loss or unsafe data downgrade occurs.

scenarios.given: the complete selected-language/platform/client fixture matrix includes semantic and fault cases
scenarios.then: every mandatory cell has a reproducible passing receipt; missing capabilities, licensing or recovery evidence block the claimed GA matrix.

scenarios.given: a warm agent session already holds the relevant context
scenarios.then: routing requests only needed new evidence; it does not reload all skills, memories or full symbol bodies solely because a turn started.

scenarios.given: many clients and a project exceed configured resource/concurrency limits
scenarios.then: requests queue, reject or degrade with explicit policy/coverage while limits remain bounded; unrelated ready work is not starved indefinitely.

scenarios.given: qualified Java Gradle/Maven fixtures plus a deferred mixed Java/Kotlin fixture and unqualified Android/KMP fixtures
scenarios.then: qualified Java cases pass across source boundaries; deferred Kotlin and unqualified project types are labeled and cannot silently count as production support or complete mixed-language references.

scenarios.given: an ordinary LSP client advertises standard WorkspaceEdit support but lacks the qualified guarded-application integration
scenarios.when: it initializes and requests rename or a mutating code action
scenarios.then: Threadnote does not advertise or return an immediately applicable mutation; navigation remains available and a preview/integration requirement is explained. A qualified first-party client exposes the action only through proposal checks, authoritative application, acknowledgement and observed-state reconciliation.

scenarios.given: a qualified multi-file operation has written its first target, then the next target text or owner changes before its conditional mutation
scenarios.then: the changed target is preserved, remaining writes stop, and the receipt reports the written target and conflict/partial outcome; recovery never duplicates the first change or overwrites the concurrent edit.

excluded.reason: P12 benchmark study; not P11 functional qualification
